paragraphs: If you’re pregnant, your care and costs are determined by your beneficiary status, how close you live to a military hospital or clinic that provides obstetric and gynecological services, and your choice of TRICARE plan and provider.
TRICARE covers the following maternity care services:

- Obstetric visits throughout your pregnancy
- Fetal ultrasounds
- Management of high-risk or complicated pregnancies
- Hospitalization for labor, delivery, and postpartum care
- Deliveries at TRICARE-certified/authorized birthing centers or deliveries planned at home (stateside only).
Note: Home births aren’t covered in overseas locations.

Active duty service members and active duty family members have no costs for maternity care when enrolled in a TRICARE Prime plan. All others (including those enrolled in TRICARE Select, TRICARE Reserve Select, TRICARE Retired Reserve, TRICARE Young Adult-Select, the Continued Health Care Benefit Program, and retirees, their family members, and all others) have copayments, cost-shares, or both. For detailed cost information, go to www.tricare.mil/costs.

Beneﬁciaries with a TRICARE Prime plan (except for ADSMs) may use the point-of-service option to self-refer to an obstetrician but will pay higher out-of-pocket costs. For more information about the POS option, go to www.tricare.mil/pointofservice.

Additional childbirth and breastfeeding services (including certain doulas and lactation specialists) are available to TRICARE Prime and TRICARE Select enrollees under the Childbirth and Breastfeeding Support Demonstration. The demonstration is available stateside and overseas. Learn more at www.tricare.mil/cbsd.
For more information on covered services, go to www.tricare.mil/coveredservices.
This brochure isn’t all-inclusive. For more information, go to www.tricare.mil.
Your guidelines for getting care vary based on your TRICARE health plan and whether you live stateside or overseas. Maternity care services may require referrals, pre-authorizations, or both.

| TRICARE Prime                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | If your primary care manager is at a military hospital or clinic with maternity care services, the military hospital or clinic will provide your maternity care. If maternity care is unavailable at your military hospital or clinic, your PCM will refer you to a civilian network provider. If you have a civilian PCM, your PCM will direct your maternity care or give you a referral to an obstetrician.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

Non-network providers may charge up to 15% above the TRICARE-allowable charge. You’re responsible for that amount, in addition to any deductible or cost-shares.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

| TRICARE Select Overseas and TRICARE Reserve Select, TRICARE Retired Reserve and Continued Health Care Benefit Program overseas                                                                                                                                    | You may seek care from almost any TRICARE-authorized civilian provider without a referral. There may be specific requirements or limitations for midwives or other provider types in overseas locations. Contact the TRICARE Overseas contractor for a benefit review and to ensure your provider is TRICARE-authorized. Overseas providers aren’t required to bill TRICARE on your behalf. You should expect to pay up front for care and submit a claim with proof of payment to get reimbursed. Outside the U.S. and U.S. territories (American Samoa, Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands, Puerto Rico, and the U.S. Virgin Islands), there may be no limit to the amount that nonparticipating non-network providers may bill. You’re responsible for paying any amount that exceeds the TRICARE-allowable charge, in addition to your deductible, cost-shares, and copayments. For more information, visit www\.tricare.mil/selectoverseas. |

Your child has separate TRICARE coverage after they’re born. However, the sponsor must register the new child in the Defense Enrollment and Eligibility Reporting Systems within 90 days (120 days if overseas) of birth, adoption, or court appointment. To do this, the sponsor must go to a Uniformed Services ID card office and present the child’s official birth certificate or FS-240 Consular Report of Birth Abroad, record of adoption, or letter of placement of your child into your home by a recognized placement or adoption agency or the court.
For children of retirees, there’s no automatic enrollment process. Within 90 days of birth, adoption, or court appointment, you must:

- Register your child in DEERS.
- Contact your regional contractor to enroll your children in a TRICARE plan.

Visit milConnect to confirm your child’s enrollment within 90 days of birth, adoption, or court appointment. After 90 days, you must wait until another QLE or TRICARE Open Season to enroll your child in a different TRICARE plan.

An ADSM has 120 days to register their new child in DEERS. Once registered, the child will automatically be enrolled in TRICARE Select Overseas. You have 90 days from the auto-enrollment date to change your newborn’s enrollment to TRICARE Prime Overseas or TRICARE Prime Remote Overseas, if eligible and command-sponsored. Otherwise, your child stays in TRICARE Select Overseas.

If the sponsor enrolls the new child in TRICARE Prime Overseas or TRICARE Prime Remote Overseas, coverage is backdated to the birth date. The family may ask the TRICARE Overseas Program contractor to reprocess any claims that were denied or should be processed under TRICARE Prime Overseas or TRICARE Prime Remote Overseas.
# TRICARE Prime® and TRICARE Select®
Once registered in DEERS, a newborn, adopted, or court-appointed child of an ADSM will be automatically enrolled in a TRICARE plan based on where the child lives.
Children of ADSMs are automatically enrolled in TRICARE Prime as long as:

- They’re registered in DEERS.
- They live in a stateside Prime Service Area. If they don’t live in a PSA, the child will be automatically enrolled in TRICARE Select.
You may choose to change your child’s coverage to another TRICARE plan, if eligible, within 90 days from the date entered in DEERS.
# TRICARE Reserve Select® and TRICARE Retired Reserve®

Your child will be covered by TRS or TRR if you purchased family coverage, registered them in DEERS, and enrolled them in TRS or TRR. Submit your child’s enrollment form to your regional contractor within 90 days (120 days if overseas) of birth or adoption. For information about covering your child with TRS or TRR family coverage, visit www.tricare.mil/trs or www.tricare.mil/trr.

A new child of a TYA member isn’t covered by TRICARE unless the child’s other parent is a sponsor or the child is adopted by a sponsor. They also won’t be able to get care at military hospitals and clinics.
# HOW TO ENROLL OR CHANGE ENROLLMENT

Once your child is registered in DEERS, you can enroll or make enrollment changes online, by phone, by mail, or in person at a TRICARE Service Center (overseas only). For details and instructions, visit www.tricare.mil/enroll.
Continued Health Care Benefit Program

If your child is born, adopted, or court appointed while you have CHCBP coverage, you may not need to register them in DEERS. Contact the CHCBP contractor, Humana Military, to enroll your child in the CHCBP. Visit www.tricare.mil/chcbp for more information.

To transfer your enrollment, you need to coordinate with your PCM to get referrals for nonemergency health care services in the location you’re visiting. To transfer your enrollment, contact your regional contractor. Overseas, different rules apply. Contact your TOP Regional Call Center for guidance.
# Children Born to Covered Family Members

If you’re a TRICARE-eligible unmarried child of a TRICARE sponsor, TRICARE will cover your pregnancy care before, during, and after childbirth. However, TRICARE doesn’t cover your new baby unless the child’s other parent is a sponsor. In certain situations, your newborn may be eligible for care under the Secretarial Designee Program, subject to the decision of your military hospital or clinic’s commander.
# IF YOU LOSE TRICARE ELIGIBILITY

You may lose TRICARE eligibility, including maternity coverage, for various reasons related to life events and sponsor status changes. Depending on the reason for losing eligibility, you may qualify for continued coverage under the Transitional Assistance Management Program or CHCBP. CHCBP requires premium payments. If you’re an ADSM who’s pregnant at the time of release from active duty, you may also work with your service (unit personnel and military hospital or clinic administrative channels) to determine if you’re eligible for ongoing care at a military hospital or clinic. Visit www.tricare.mil/maternitycare for more information.
